chung.Syllabus Name: Digital Signal Processing_Xử lý tín hiệu số
chung.Learning-Teaching Method: In-class lecture, Active Learning, Social Constructivism, Project-Based Learning
chung.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
chung.Description: Digital Signal Processing (DSP) is a fundamental course that provides undergraduate engineering students with core theoretical knowledge and practical techniques for the analysis, processing, and design of discrete-time signal processing systems. The course covers discrete-time signals and systems, sampling theory, the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) and Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), digital filter design using FIR and IIR structures, quadrature (I/Q) signal representation, and practical DSP implementation techniques. Upon completion of the course, students will be able to analyze signal spectra, design digital filters, and apply DSP methods to engineering applications such as digital communications, measurement systems, audio signal processing, and embedded systems.
chung.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact sessions in order to be accepted to the final examination.
- Student is responsible to do all exercises and practical given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time. Do quizzes during class.
- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose
- Promptly access to the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information

taiLieu: Digital Signal Processing: Principles, Algorithms, and Applications (5th Edition)

John G. Proakis
Dimitris G. Manolakis
Prentice Hall International / Prentice Hall, Inc.
clo: Knowledge - demonstrate an understanding of fundamental digital signal processing concepts, including discrete-time signals, linear time-invariant (LTI) systems, sampling, DFT/FFT, digital FIR and IIR filters, and quadrature signal processing.
Analysis - analyze discrete-time signals in both the time and frequency domains, and evaluate the effects of sampling, aliasing, windowing, and spectral resolution.
Design - design and compare digital FIR and IIR filters to meet specified technical requirements, and select appropriate filter structures for given engineering applications.
Application - apply core DSP algorithms and selected practical DSP techniques to solve real-world engineering problems.
Technical Skills - use engineering software tools (such as MATLAB, Python, or equivalent platforms) to model, simulate, and evaluate digital signal processing systems.
